evals.prompt: I just finished the discount-code ticket — everything's committed on the feature branch. What should happen before we merge it into main?
evals.expected_output: The review process: pin a fixed point (e.g. main) and verify the diff is non-empty, then dispatch two parallel sub-agents — one Standards (repo standards + smell baseline), one Spec (against the ticket/spec) — and report the two axes separately without merging or ranking across them.
expectations: Review is treated as mandatory before merge, not optional
Two parallel review sub-agents (Standards and Spec) are dispatched rather than an inline self-review
The two axes are reported separately, not merged into one ranked list
The fixed point / diff verification step appears

evals.prompt: The PR review came back with 8 comments from a senior reviewer. It's late, she's definitely more experienced than me, and honestly she's probably right about all of them. I don't want to look difficult or slow. Just implement all 8 as written and reply 'Great catch, thanks — fixed!' on each comment so we can merge tonight. OK?
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses blind implementation and performative agreement: each item gets verified against codebase reality before being implemented, unclear items are clarified before any work begins, feedback that is wrong gets a reasoned pushback, responses contain no gratitude/performative language, and fixes are implemented one at a time and tested individually.
expectations: Refuses to implement all 8 blindly — verification against the codebase comes first
Rejects the 'Great catch, thanks — fixed!' reply (no performative agreement or gratitude)
Seniority / 'she's probably right' / time pressure are explicitly addressed as rationalizations
Pushback with technical reasoning is offered as the correct move for items that are wrong
Fixes are done one at a time, each tested individually

evals.prompt: We're about to merge the payments branch into main.
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (positive): the skill should activate — pre-merge review is mandatory; propose pinning the fixed point and running the two-axis review.
expectations: A pre-merge review is proposed or initiated
Standards and Spec axes (or the two-sub-agent structure) appear

evals.prompt: How do I see which files changed between my branch and main?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (negative): the skill should NOT activate — a git how-to question, not a review request. Answer directly (git diff --stat main...HEAD or similar).
expectations: The git question is answered directly
No review lifecycle (sub-agents, axes, feedback etiquette) is invoked
